_meta.indication: QULIPTA is indicated for the preventive treatment of episodic migraine in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study; patients randomized 1:1:1:1 to placebo, atogepant 10 mg QD, 30 mg QD, or 60 mg QD over a 12-week double-blind treatment period.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with a history of episodic migraine (4 to 14 migraine days per month), with approximately 70% required to have taken at least one prior migraine preventive medication.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in mean monthly migraine days across the 12-week double-blind treatment period.
pivotal_trials.result: Mean change from baseline in monthly migraine days: -3.7 (10 mg), -3.9 (30 mg), -4.2 (60 mg) vs -2.5 placebo; differences from placebo -1.2, -1.4, -1.7 respectively (adjusted p<0.0001 for all doses).

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group dose-finding study; patients randomized in a 2:1:2:1:2:1 sequence to placebo, atogepant 10 mg QD, 30 mg QD, 30 mg BID, 60 mg QD, or 60 mg BID over a 12-week double-blind treatment period.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with a history of episodic migraine (4 to 14 migraine days per month); unlike Study 1, prior preventive medication use was not required (only about 30% had tried a prior preventive).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in mean monthly migraine days across the 12-week double-blind treatment period.
pivotal_trials.n: 834 randomized (652 in the QD/placebo arms carried into the labeled efficacy analysis)
pivotal_trials.result: Mean change from baseline in monthly migraine days: -4.0 (10 mg), -3.8 (30 mg), -3.6 (60 mg) vs -2.8 placebo; differences from placebo -1.1, -0.9, -0.7 respectively; all three QD doses statistically significant versus placebo after multiplicity adjustment.

key_safety: The most common adverse reactions (incidence at least 4% and greater than placebo) are nausea, constipation, and fatigue. In Studies 1 and 2 nausea occurred in 5-9% of atogepant patients (vs 3% placebo), constipation 6% (vs 1%), and fatigue/somnolence 4-6% (vs 3%); no deaths and no serious adverse events with a clear association with atogepant.
target_moa: Atogepant is an orally-administered calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) receptor antagonist; CGRP plays an important role in migraine attacks, and CGRP antagonists have been shown to alleviate migraine symptoms.

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the clinical trial design was acceptable, the efficacy findings were clear, and the safety profile was acceptable for use in the intended population.

description.text: Expanded QULIPTA's indication for preventive treatment of migraine in adults to include chronic migraine, adding a 60 mg once-daily dosage for chronic migraine.

citations.quote: For chronic migraine, the recommended dosage is 60 mg taken once daily. (2.1)

summary.text: Atogepant's NDA was submitted by AbbVie and received a priority review designation based on the Applicant's use of a Material Threat Countermeasure Priority Review Voucher; it was approved first cycle for the preventive treatment of episodic migraine in adults, was not referred to an advisory committee, and was not granted accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, or orphan designation.

citations.quote: This new drug application (NDA) for atogepant was submitted by AbbVie, Inc. (the Applicant). Atogepant is an oral small molecule calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) receptor antagonist, developed for the preventive treatment of episodic migraine (EM) in adults.
This NDA received a priority review designation because of the Applicant's use of a Material Threat Countermeasure Priority Review Voucher.

This application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the clinical trial design was acceptable, the efficacy findings were clear, and the safety profile was acceptable for use in the intended population.
